summary: Mixed-variant batch job billed at non-quantized rate despite quantized model in job manifest
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that a scheduled nightly batch (UUID: bch-20260311-9f3) submitted as a mixed-variant job was charged at the non-quantized (FP16) per-token rate for the entire run. The job manifest and console job details show the primary model specified as redwood-v1-quantized-8bit with a small fallback variant rwkv-13b-fp16 for longer-context segments. Impact:
- Customer saw a ~2.4x increase on the batch invoice line versus cost estimate for that run (~$6.1k billed vs $2.5k expected).
- This affects their month-to-date spend forecast and triggers an alert with their finance team.
Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dedicated-eu-west-2a (customer pinned capacity) but job executed in prod|us-west-2 due to routing policy for burst coverage.
- Job type: asynchronous batch embedding + generation with model switching enabled in the job manifest.
Steps to reproduce (from customer's job):
1) Submit batch job with manifest specifying primary model redwood-v1-quantized-8bit and fallback rwkv-13b-fp16 for segments > 4096 tokens.
2) Observe console that the serving runtime selected the quantized model for 78% of segments and non-quantized for 22% of segments.
3) Review invoice line for job bch-20260311-9f3 and compare to Console estimate.
Expected behavior:
- Billing should pro-rate the per-token rate by the actual model variant used for each inference (quantized tokens billed at quantized rate, FP16 tokens billed at FP16 rate).
Actual behavior:
- Invoice shows a single blended rate equivalent to the FP16 model for the entire job, effectively charging FP16 price for all tokens.
Logs/Artifacts provided by customer:
- Console job export (job-manifest.json) attached by customer (they provided download link).
- Screenshot of Console model usage overview showing variant split 78/22.
- Invoice excerpt (line 42) showing charge of $6,112.30 for job bch-20260311-9f3.
- Customer-provided estimate ($2,545.00) from Console before run.
Notes:
- Customer has dedicated plan with reserved capacity; they expect reserved/quantized pricing to apply where the quantized variant is actually used.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Postback composer bug emits single highest-cost rate-class when traces span multiple runtime pools (observed in postback logs).
Hypothesis 2: Routing fallback to hosted pool without quantized variant caused job-level metadata to be stamped as FP16 and downstream billing to ignore per-request variant tags.

Query results: SELECT count(*) FROM postbacks WHERE job_id='bch-20260311-9f3' returned 128 postback rows; 100 rows have variant_tag='quantized', 28 rows variant_tag='fp16', but aggregate.rate_class_id is 'rate_fp16_2026_q1'.
Reproducer: Simulated mixed-variant run across two pools in staging and observed composer behavior reproducing incorrect rate-class selection. Added unit test that fails on current composer logic.
Related signals: See incident SUP-901111 where a similar but lower-severity issue occurred during regional failover; composer logic was noted but not fixed then.
Temporary mitigation: Engineering suggested changing routing policy to prefer pools with matching quantized variants for customers on dedicated plans to avoid cross-pool mixing until fix is deployed.
resolution: (pending) provisional credit applied. Root cause identified: postback composer that aggregates per-request variant tags into job-level invoice lines erroneously collapses to the highest-cost variant when traces span multiple serving pools. Fix implemented in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/prs/1287 to emit per-variant line items and preserve per-request variant tags. Deployment plan: staged rollout to billing composer service with canary in prod (5% traffic) on 2026-03-14, full rollout 2026-03-15 after monitoring. Post-deployment actions: recompose historic postbacks for affected window (2026-03-11 00:00Z - 2026-03-12 06:00Z) to generate corrected invoice lines and finalize credit. Customer notified and provisional credit applied pending reconciliation. Follow-up: postmortem to be published and linked to ticket after reconciliation completes.
